Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
revision_notes: Fetched cited RISE ESMAP page: it shows Egypt has no formal decentralised-energy electrification plan under the planning sub-indicator, but this is a narrow sub-indicator and does not capture Egypt's actual off-grid regulatory activity, so the original score of 1 (No policy framework) understates the position. Searches found EgyptERA Circular No. 3 of 2023, in force since January 2023, which sets licensing, capacity-cap (up to 1,000 MW nationally) and periodic reporting rules specifically for off-grid self-consumption solar systems. Also found that EgyptERA formally adopted a dedicated Smart Mini-Grids Regulatory Package in 2025 (developed with the Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy and the EU-funded MENALINKS programme), covering licensing, tariffs and ownership models for renewable mini-grids in rural/remote areas. Together these represent an active regulatory framework with some deployment already occurring under the 2023 self-consumption circular, though mini-grid investment specifically is only beginning following the 2025 adoption; MENALINKS itself describes mini-grids as still an 'untapped opportunity'. Recalculated to 3 = Active policy with some deployment, per the metadata scale. Not top-of-scale, so no human review flag required.
revised_comments: Egypt has an established and active regulatory framework for off-grid and distributed energy. The Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA)'s Circular No. 3 of 2023 sets out licensing, capacity and periodic reporting rules for off-grid self-consumption solar systems, with a national capacity cap of 1,000 MW and requirements for monthly and quarterly compliance reporting by network operators. In 2025, EgyptERA formally adopted a dedicated Smart Mini-Grids Regulatory Package, developed jointly with the Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy and the EU-funded MENALINKS programme, establishing licensing, tariff-setting and ownership rules for renewable-based mini-grids intended to serve rural and remote communities. Off-grid self-consumption solar deployment is already under way under the 2023 circular, while private investment in mini-grids specifically remains at an early stage following the 2025 regulatory adoption.
